findings.detail: In a default stdout Scrut block, `{ some-command 2>&1; } 01>/dev/null` passes without a reason while discarding the child's stderr. The enclosing stdout descriptor is compared with the literal string "1" before normalization, so its capture state is not propagated. The nested command consequently treats descriptor 1 as live Scrut output. The sibling `{ some-command 2>&1; } 1<>/dev/null` also escapes because the propagation operator list omits `<>`. Propagate the actual descriptor destinations, or conservatively reject unsupported inherited destinations, before granting live-forwarding exceptions.
findings.evidence: Static trace: line 31 does not recognize N.Value "01" or operator "<>" as retained stdout. The enclosing redirect changes only descriptor 1, so lines 64-65 emit no stderr finding. Recursion at lines 78-81 passes captured=false; line 41 initializes the child's descriptor 1 as "stdout" again. Its 2>&1 therefore resolves to "stdout" and is filtered out by line 65. Descriptor normalization at line 44 applies only to the separate local redirect reduction. Existing leading-zero tests cover direct descriptor-2 operations, not inherited stdout destinations.
findings.title: Sibling input forms: inherited stdout redirects bypass Scrut's live-forwarding rule

findings.detail: An unavailable upstream lookup still becomes a successful empty result. When the remaining lookups find no drift, the script exits successfully with empty stdout, and the repository workflow closes an existing drift issue despite the incomplete audit. Keeping stderr live does not prevent that incorrect action. This predates the supplied base and retains the previously recorded Important severity.
findings.evidence: The Node lookup at lines 66-70 converts failure to an empty latest value and returns successfully; the other lookup helpers repeat this handling. print_report emits nothing when drift_rows is empty. .github/workflows/version-audit.yml sets has_drift=false for empty stdout and then closes the existing audit issue. Reading bin/version-audit at e8667c85610d10882e7c33078748c7113b1c4a8e confirms the same failure-to-empty behavior before this change.
findings.title: Absent or partial data: upstream failures still become a no-drift success
